meta.description: Machine-readable reverse-engineering of the current CMS Medicaid Enterprise Systems (MES) APD template set, mandatory since 2026-07-01 under SHO #25-003. Every section carries: what content is required, by which APD type, which federal provision demands it, what a CMS State Officer looks for, and the machine-checkable rules that prove it is satisfied. This artifact is the spine of APD Studio; the Authoring Workspace, Compliance Validator, Budget Engine, and AoA Builder all reference section ids and rule ids defined here.

sections.reviewerFocus: This is the heart of the enhanced-match case. A State Officer reads the explanations, not the checkboxes.

conditions.text: CMS determines the system is likely to provide more efficient, economical, and effective administration of the State plan.
The system meets the system requirements, standards and conditions, and performance standards in Part 11 of the State Medicaid Manual, as periodically amended.

The system is compatible with the claims processing and information retrieval systems used in the administration of Medicare for prompt eligibility verification and for processing claims for persons eligible for both programs.
The system supports the data requirements of quality improvement organizations established under Part B of title XI of the Act.
The State owns any software that is designed, developed, installed or improved with 90 percent FFP.

The Department has a royalty free, non-exclusive, and irrevocable license to reproduce, publish, or otherwise use and authorize others to use, for Federal Government purposes, software, modifications to software, and documentation that is designed, developed, installed or enhanced with 90 percent FFP.
The costs of the system are determined in accordance with 2 CFR parts 200 and 300, subpart E.

The Medicaid agency agrees in writing to use the system for the period of time specified in the advance planning document approved by CMS or for any shorter period of time that CMS determines justifies the Federal funds invested.
The agency agrees in writing that the information in the system will be safeguarded in accordance with subpart F, part 431 of this subchapter.

Use a modular, flexible approach to systems development, including the use of open interfaces and exposed application programming interfaces; the separation of business rules from core programming, available in both human and machine readable formats.
Align to, and advance increasingly, in MITA maturity for business, architecture, and data.
conditions.note: Names no specific maturity level and no required rate of advancement. There is no numeric threshold to validate against. See CONFLICT-006 on the MITA State Self-Assessment.

conditions.text: The agency ensures alignment with, and incorporation of, standards and implementation specifications for health information technology adopted by the Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT in 45 CFR part 170, subpart B. The agency also ensures alignment with: the HIPAA privacy, security, breach notification and enforcement regulations in 45 CFR parts 160 and 164; and the transaction standards and operating rules adopted by the Secretary under HIPAA and/or section 1104 of the Affordable Care Act. The agency meets accessibility standards established under section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act, or standards that provide greater accessibility for individuals with disabilities, and compliance with Federal civil rights laws; standards and protocols adopted by the Secretary under section 1561 of the Affordable Care Act; standards and protocols for reporting on the Child and Adult Core Sets as adopted by the Secretary under sections 1139A, 1139B, and 1902(a)(6) of the Act, and 42 CFR part 437 subpart A; and standards and protocols for reporting on the Health Home Core Sets as adopted by the Secretary under sections 1902(a)(6), 1945(c)(4)(B) and (g), and 1945A(g) of the Act and 42 CFR part 437 subpart A.
Promote sharing, leverage, and reuse of Medicaid technologies and systems within and among States.
Support accurate and timely processing and adjudications/eligibility determinations and effective communications with providers, beneficiaries, and the public.

conditions.text: The system supports seamless coordination and integration with the Marketplace, the Federal Data Services Hub, and allows interoperability with health information exchanges, public health agencies, human services programs, and community organizations providing outreach and enrollment assistance services as applicable.

For E&E systems, the State must have delivered acceptable MAGI-based system functionality, demonstrated by performance testing and results based on critical success factors, with limited mitigations and workarounds.
The State must submit plans that contain strategies for reducing the operational consequences of failure to meet applicable requirements for all major milestones and functionality.

Systems and modules developed, installed or improved with 90 percent match must include documentation of components and procedures such that the systems could be operated by a variety of contractors or other users.

For software systems and modules developed, installed or improved with 90 percent match, the State must consider strategies to minimize the costs and difficulty of operating the software on alternate hardware or operating systems.

evaluationCriteria.table: Table E: Example Alternatives Analysis Criteria

criteria.name: Reuse
criteria.description: Solution adapts existing capabilities within the state, capabilities in use by another state, or those available from the vendor community, with minimal customization and/or incorporates reuse into the design of new capabilities.

criteria.name: Functionality
criteria.description: Solution meets the technical requirements and functional specifications identified by the state. (Each alternative may be scored against multiple requirements.)

criteria.name: Cost
criteria.description: The solution is evaluated for its total cost of ownership, including design, development, testing, training, migration, implementation, licensing, and operations and maintenance.

criteria.name: Benefits
criteria.description: Solution meets non-financial business needs. (Use the benefits identified from the analysis summarized in Section 1.)

criteria.name: Risks
criteria.description: Expectations for the overall solution risk are low. (Each alternative may be scored against multiple risks.)

criteria.name: Scalability
criteria.description: Solution can effectively and efficiently scale with the project's growth and changing needs.

criteria.name: Ease of Implementation
criteria.description: Solution can be implemented without disrupting existing operations.

criteria.name: Vendor Experience
criteria.description: The vendor providing the solution has experience, client references, and a demonstrated history of similar MES implementations.

criteria.name: User Experience
criteria.description: Solution is user friendly, and the end users will not require extensive ongoing training.

criteria.name: Innovation Potential
criteria.description: Solution is well-positioned to support future technical enhancements and leverages modern tools/technology stacks.

criteria.name: Organizational Impact
criteria.description: Solution can be supported by the current organizational and personnel structure and constraints.

criteria.name: Schedule
criteria.description: Solution will be implemented within a time frame that meets the business needs.

criteria.name: Maintainability
criteria.description: Solution will not be difficult or costly to maintain.

criteria.name: Security
criteria.description: Solution will conform to government and industry security standards.

criteria.name: Accessibility
criteria.description: Solution meets accessibility standards established under Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act or standards that provide greater accessibility for individuals with disabilities and comply with federal civil rights laws.

evaluationMatrix.cellInstruction: Score (per Scoring Guide), then multiply by weight.

reuseRule.finding: Reuse is a MANDATORY SCORING CRITERION, not a mandatory alternative.
reuseRule.detail: Reuse is criterion #1 in Table E and Section 3 states criteria 'must include' reuse. Section 2.2 requires describing reuse alternatives evaluated and, if none were viable, explaining why. No template text requires that one of the enumerated alternatives BE a transfer/reuse option.
reuseRule.productImplication: The Compliance Validator must check for the reuse criterion and the why-not explanation, NOT for the presence of a reuse alternative. Getting this distinction wrong produces false failures.

validationRules.check: MINIMUM ALTERNATIVES. If a legacy solution exists, the AoA covers the current state plus at least two proposed alternatives. If no legacy solution exists, at least three alternatives.

REUSE WHY-NOT. If no reuse option was viable, an explicit written explanation is present in Section 2.2.
REQUIRED CRITERIA. Evaluation criteria include, at minimum, reuse, functionality, cost, benefits, and risks.
validationRules.basis: AoA template Section 3: criteria 'must include but aren't limited to reuse functionality, cost, benefits, and risks'

validationRules.check: SCORING CONSISTENCY. Every alternative is scored against every criterion; no blank cells in the evaluation matrix.

validationRules.check: MATRIX ARITHMETIC. If weights are applied, every weighted score equals score x weight, column totals equal the sum of weighted scores, and Solution Rank is consistent with the totals.
validationRules.basis: AoA template Table I cell instruction

validationRules.check: PREFERRED SOLUTION CONSISTENCY. The preferred solution in Section 6 is the top-ranked alternative in the Section 5 matrix, or a written justification explains the departure.

knownConflicts.severity: HIGH — affects the AoA Builder's output target
knownConflicts.title: SHO #25-003 and the published templates disagree on where the AoA goes

sourceA.quote: States will be expected to use the template to complete Section 5 of the new MES APD and/or Appendix A of the new MES OAPD.

sourceB.quote: During the PAPD, only a commitment to perform the AoA is required via Section 3. The AoA should be completed and included as part of the initial IAPD (typically referenced within Section 3 and included via Appendix B).

sourceC.finding: Section 3 is 'Requirements Analysis, Feasibility Study, Analysis of Alternatives Considerations' and directs the reader to Appendix B for the complete AoA. Section 5 is 'Acquisitions'.

sourceD.finding: Appendix A is 'Proposed Activity Schedule for the Project'. No AoA reference appears in OAPD Appendices A through D.

knownConflicts.assessment: The most likely explanation is that SHO #25-003 described the AoA's placement against a draft template numbering that changed before publication. The published templates plus the FAQ are internally consistent with each other and inconsistent with the SHO.
knownConflicts.resolution: BUILD AGAINST THE PUBLISHED TEMPLATES AND THE FAQ: AoA lives at APD Section 3 (reference) plus Appendix B (full document). Surface the SHO's conflicting sentence to the user rather than hiding it. Confirm with a CMS MES State Officer.
knownConflicts.productImpact: The AoA Builder must not write into APD Section 5 or OAPD Appendix A. Note the project's own standing instructions currently repeat the SHO's Section 5 / OAPD Appendix A framing — that should be corrected.

knownConflicts.severity: LOW — cosmetic but it will break a field mapping
knownConflicts.title: Appendix C table letter ambiguity
knownConflicts.detail: The retrieved PRA conversion of the MES APD template renders the Appendix C instruction as referring to 'Table J' while separately labeling the CEF grid 'Table K'. Table J is the Section 12 Assurances table. One of these is an extraction artifact.
knownConflicts.resolution: Confirm the actual table letter against the Word original before hard-coding it into the field mapping.

knownConflicts.title: Cost principles citation — OMB Circular A-87 vs 2 CFR Part 200
knownConflicts.detail: The MES APD template Section 10 instructs states to follow 45 CFR 95.507 and OMB Circular A-87. OMB Circular A-87 was superseded by 2 CFR Part 200. Both 42 CFR 433.112(b)(7) ('in accordance with 2 CFR parts 200 and 300, subpart E') and 45 CFR 95.613(a) point to 2 CFR parts 200 and 300.
knownConflicts.resolution: Draft to 2 CFR Part 200 while reproducing the template's own citation where the template requires it. Do not assert to a customer that the template's A-87 citation is an error without confirming with a State Officer.

knownConflicts.title: OAPD length — regulation says two pages, template is longer
knownConflicts.detail: 45 CFR 95.610(c)(3) describes the Operational APDU as 'no more than two pages' containing summary of activities, acquisitions, and annual budget by project/system. The current CMS MES OAPD template has three numbered sections plus four appendices and is materially longer.
knownConflicts.resolution: The template governs in practice. Note the tension; do not tell a customer their OAPD must be two pages.

knownConflicts.severity: MEDIUM — affects Budget Engine validation logic
knownConflicts.title: MDBT V1.06 shows a 90 percent M&O column
knownConflicts.detail: See mdbt.anomaly. 42 CFR 433.116(a) sets operations FFP at 75 percent.
knownConflicts.resolution: Flag 90 percent M&O for human review rather than auto-failing until the real .xlsx is opened and V1.09 is obtained.

knownConflicts.severity: MEDIUM — affects whether a MITA SS-A check exists at all
knownConflicts.title: The MITA State Self-Assessment obligation was removed from current guidance but not repealed
knownConflicts.detail: SMC Guidance v1.0 (April 2022) contained a 'MITA STATE SELF-ASSESSMENTS' section requiring the SS-A. SMC Guidance v2.0 (October 21, 2025) deleted it. SHO #25-003, its FAQ, and the current MES APD template never mention MITA or the SS-A outside CEF 11. Meanwhile the MITA Governance Board FAQ still states states 'are required to submit a MITA SS-A in support of their request for enhanced federal matching,' citing 42 CFR 433.112(b)(11) and 433.116(b), (c), and (i). The 'What Changed' crosswalk does not mention MITA at all, so CMS did not document this as a deliberate removal.
knownConflicts.resolution: Do NOT build a hard 'SS-A attached?' gate. Make it a configurable, state-specific check with the conflict surfaced. The only durable citable MITA obligation is CEF 11.
knownConflicts.additionalFinding: There is no CMS primary source for an ANNUAL SS-A cadence. CIB 07/05/2013 states a one-time trigger (within twelve months of MITA 3.0 release); CIB 08/05/2014 says CMS 'is encouraging' completion and 'Upon receipt of state submission, CMS will consider this requirement met.' The widely repeated 'annually' figure traces to state and vendor documents, not CMS. Labeled ASSUMPTION.

knownConflicts.severity: MEDIUM — affects the Ongoing Obligations Engine
knownConflicts.title: Operational reporting cadence — the annual OAPD-supporting report may or may not survive
knownConflicts.detail: SHO #25-003's cadence/frequency distinction resolves the monthly-vs-quarterly EVV question cleanly. What remains unresolved is whether the annual OAPD-supporting operational report from SMDL #22-001 and SMC Guidance v1.0 is a surviving separate obligation or was replaced by the monthly ORW. CMS's own Certification Repository states both: the Ongoing Reporting index says annual, the Ongoing Reporting Overview says monthly AND quarterly EVV AND annual with OAPD requests.
knownConflicts.resolution: Encode monthly ORW submission for non-EVV, quarterly for EVV on the Table 2 calendar, monthly capture throughout, monthly PSR through DDI and post-certification. Flag the annual-OAPD question as an open item requiring CMS MES State Officer confirmation. Never assert a flat 'everything is monthly'.
